translation_en: Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘A woman should not fast while her husband is present without his permission.’

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Ibn Abi ‘Adi narrated to us, from Shu‘bah, from Sulayman, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘When a man calls his wife to his bed and she refuses to come, the angels curse her until morning.’

Muhammad ibn ‘Ar‘arah narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Zurarah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘When a woman spends the night abandoning her husband’s bed, the angels curse her until she returns.’

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us: Shu‘ayb informed us: Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘It is not lawful for a woman to fast while her husband is present without his permission, or to admit anyone into his house without his permission. Whatever she spends from his property without his instruction, half of it is returned to him.’ Abu al-Zinad also narrated it, from Musa, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, concerning the fast.

Musaddad narrated to us: Isma‘il narrated to us: Al-Taymi informed us, from Abu ‘Uthman, from Usamah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘I stood at the gate of Paradise, and most of those who entered it were the poor, while the wealthy were held back. The people of the Fire had already been ordered to the Fire. Then I stood at the gate of the Fire, and most of those who entered it were women.’

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Malik informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. The Messenger of Allah prayed, and the people prayed with him. He stood for a long time, about as long as it takes to recite Surah al-Baqarah. Then he bowed for a long time, rose and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing, then bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing, and then prostrated. Then he stood and stood for a long time, less than the first standing, then bowed for a long time, less than the first bowing, then rose and stood for a long time, less than the first standing, then bowed for a long time, less than the first bowing, then rose and prostrated. He then finished, and the sun had become clear. He said, ‘The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs; they do not eclipse because of anyone’s death or life. When you see that, remember Allah.’ They said, ‘Messenger of Allah, we saw you reach for something from where you stood, then we saw you draw back.’ He said, ‘I saw—or was shown—Paradise, and I reached for a cluster of its fruit. Had I taken it, you would have eaten from it for as long as the world remained. I also saw the Fire, and I have never seen a sight like it today. I saw that most of its people were women.’ They asked, ‘Why, Messenger of Allah?’ He said, ‘Because of their ingratitude.’ It was asked, ‘Do they disbelieve in Allah?’ He said, ‘They are ungrateful to their husbands and ungrateful for kindness. If you were kind to one of them throughout a lifetime, then she saw one thing from you, she would say, “I have never seen any good from you.”’

‘Uthman ibn al-Haytham narrated to us: ‘Awf narrated to us, from Abu Raja’, from ‘Imran, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘I looked into Paradise and saw that most of its people were the poor. I looked into the Fire and saw that most of its people were women.’ Ayyub and Sallam ibn Zarir also related it.

Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Al-Awza‘i informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to me: Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman narrated to me: ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘‘Abd Allah, have I not been told that you fast during the day and pray at night?’ I said, ‘Yes, Messenger of Allah.’ He said, ‘Do not do that. Fast and break your fast; pray and sleep. Your body has a right over you, your eyes have a right over you, and your wife has a right over you.’’

‘Abdan narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah informed us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock. The ruler is a shepherd; a man is a shepherd over his household; and a woman is a shepherd over her husband’s house and his children. Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock.’

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Humayd narrated to me, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, swore to stay away from his wives for a month and remained in an upper room of his. He came down after 29 days. It was said to him, ‘Messenger of Allah, you swore to stay away for a month.’ He said, ‘A month is 29 days.’

Abu ‘Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj. Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to me: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Yahya ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Sayfi informed me that ‘Ikrimah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith told him that Umm Salamah informed him that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, swore that he would not visit some of his wives for a month. When 29 days had passed, he went to them in the morning or evening. It was said to him, ‘Prophet of Allah, you swore not to visit them for a month.’ He said, ‘A month can be 29 days.’

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Marwan ibn Mu‘awiyah narrated to us: Abu Ya‘fur narrated to us, saying: While we were discussing this with Abu al-Duha, he said: Ibn ‘Abbas narrated to us: One morning, the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, were weeping, with their families beside each of them. I went out to the mosque and found it full of people. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab came and went up to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who was in an upper room of his. ‘Umar greeted him, but no one answered. He greeted him a second time, but no one answered. He greeted him a third time, but no one answered. Then he called out, entered to see the Prophet, and asked, ‘Have you divorced your wives?’ He said, ‘No, but I have sworn to stay away from them for a month.’ He remained apart for 29 days, then went in to his wives.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Zam‘ah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘None of you should flog his wife as he would flog a slave, then have intercourse with her at the end of the day.’

Khallad ibn Yahya narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Nafi‘ narrated to us, from al-Hasan—namely, Ibn Muslim—from Safiyyah, from ‘A’ishah, that an Ansari woman married off her daughter, whose hair then fell out. She came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and mentioned this to him. She said, ‘Her husband has told me to add hair to hers.’ He said, ‘No. The women who add hair have been cursed.’

Muhammad ibn Salam narrated to us: Abu Mu‘awiyah informed us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, concerning the verse, ‘If a woman fears ill treatment or neglect from her husband…’ (4:128). She said: This refers to a woman who is with a man who no longer desires her and wants to divorce her and marry another woman. She says to him, ‘Keep me and do not divorce me; then marry someone else. You are free of any obligation to spend on me or to allot me a turn.’ That is what Allah Most High means when He says, ‘There is no blame upon them if they make a settlement between themselves, and settlement is best’ (4:128).

Musaddad narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir, who said: We practiced coitus interruptus during the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: ‘Amr informed me that ‘Ata’ heard Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, say: We practiced coitus interruptus while the Quran was being revealed. ‘Amr also narrated it, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir, who said: We practiced coitus interruptus during the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, while the Quran was being revealed.

‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma’ narrated to us: Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn Muhayriz, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said: We obtained captives and practiced coitus interruptus. We asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, about it, and he said, ‘Do you really do that?’ He said this three times. ‘There is no soul destined to come into existence until the Day of Resurrection except that it will come into existence.’

Abu Nu‘aym narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Ayman narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated to me, from al-Qasim, from ‘A’ishah, that when the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, set out, he drew lots among his wives. The lot fell to ‘A’ishah and Hafsah. At night, the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would travel with ‘A’ishah and talk with her. Hafsah said, ‘Will you ride my camel tonight and I will ride yours, so that you can see and I can see?’ She said, ‘Yes.’ So Hafsah mounted it. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came to ‘A’ishah’s camel with Hafsah on it, greeted her, then continued traveling until they stopped. ‘A’ishah missed him. When they stopped, she put her feet among the idhkhir grass and said, ‘My Lord, send a scorpion or snake against me to bite me, for I cannot say anything to him.’

Malik ibn Isma‘il narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, that Sawdah bint Zam‘ah gave her day to ‘A’ishah, and the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, allotted to ‘A’ishah her own day and Sawdah’s day.

Musaddad narrated to us: Bishr narrated to us: Khalid narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him. He said: I could say that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said this, but rather he said, ‘The Sunnah is that when a man marries a virgin, he stays with her for seven days; when he marries a previously married woman, he stays with her for three days.’

Yusuf ibn Rashid narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Sufyan. Ayyub and Khalid narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, who said: It is Sunnah that when a man marries a virgin while already married to a previously married woman, he stays with the virgin for seven days and then divides his time equally. When he marries a previously married woman while already married to a virgin, he stays with her for three days and then divides his time equally. Abu Qilabah said: If I wished, I could say that Anas attributed it to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. ‘Abd al-Razzaq said: Sufyan informed us, from Ayyub and Khalid. Khalid said, ‘If I wished, I could say that he attributed it to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.’

‘Abd al-A‘la ibn Hammad narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ narrated to us: Sa‘id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that Anas ibn Malik told them that the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, used to visit all his wives during one night, and at that time he had nine wives.

Farwah narrated to us: ‘Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, finished the afternoon prayer, he would visit his wives and draw near to one of them. He entered Hafsah’s room and stayed there longer than he usually stayed.

Isma‘il narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to me, saying: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah informed me, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that during the illness in which the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, died, he would ask, ‘Where will I be tomorrow? Where will I be tomorrow?’ He meant, ‘On whose day will I be?’ His wives gave him permission to stay wherever he wished, so he remained in ‘A’ishah’s house until he died there. ‘A’ishah said: He died on the day when it was my turn, in my house. Allah took him while his head was between my chest and neck, and his saliva mixed with mine.

‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Sulayman narrated to us, from Yahya, from ‘Ubayd ibn Hunayn, who heard Ibn ‘Abbas, from ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them all: He went in to Hafsah and said, ‘My daughter, do not be deceived because this woman, whose beauty amazes her, is loved by the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him’—meaning ‘A’ishah. I related this to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and he smiled.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Hisham, from Fatimah, from Asma’, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Yahya narrated to us, from Hisham: Fatimah narrated to me, from Asma’, that a woman said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I have a co-wife. Would it be a sin for me to make it appear that my husband has given me more than he actually has?’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘The one who boasts of what she has not been given is like someone wearing two garments of falsehood.’

‘Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Al-A‘mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from ‘Abd Allah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘No one has greater protective jealousy than Allah. For that reason, He has forbidden shameful deeds, and no one loves praise more than Allah.’

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah narrated to us, from Malik, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘O community of Muhammad, no one is more protective than Allah when He sees His male or female servant committing adultery. O community of Muhammad, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much.’

Musa ibn Isma‘il narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, that ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to him from his mother, Asma’, who heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say, ‘There is nothing more protective than Allah.’
